reader_summary.headline: My guest today is Sarah Guo, founder and managing partner of Conviction.
reader_summary.overview: My guest today is Sarah Guo, founder and managing partner of Conviction, the venture firm she built to back AI-native companies from their earliest days. Sarah has become one of the most sought-after early-stage investors in AI, often the first check into the companies defining the frontier. In this conversation, we go inside that frontier: what the small group of people actually building AI believe right now.

key_points.text: In this conversation, we go inside that frontier: what the small group of people actually building AI believe right now.
At the center is Sarah's conviction that no single company will own the future of AI, and what that means for founders, investors.
Our managing editor Dom Cooke wrote a profile of Sarah for Colossus.

So, where to begin what will hopefully be a really fun conversation? I guess because you and I are interested in so many of the same things, I'm curious what's on your mind today. I think we're both feeling a little frenzied and it's been going for a while and it feels like if anything, it might get more frenzied and more chaotic, both for what you do, but also the world around what you do. So just in this moment, what does it feel like? What's on your mind?

 Sarah 
An obvious thing for anyone thinking about how to navigate this period as an investor is just, how does it unfurl and how's it different from the past? What do I do if I can't backtest? I was talking to an investor friend last night, and the analogy he gave me was, I keep saying I wanna press the brakes as hard as I can, but I'm not doing it — I'm going 90 miles an hour. And I do think the question is, do you miss the opportunity on one side, or do you make the mistake of every boom-bust cycle in technology history? Especially if you combine that with what does it mean when you're also four years into building a firm, for the durability of the firm and the careers of the people, I think is a complex question.
